application_details.scheme_name: Royal Free Hospital Emergency Generator Replacement

waste_details.reason_for_no_provision: This is an application for elements associated to the hospital generators (enhanced and with more efficiency), so there is no waste material anticipated.

subdivision_of_building: The project includes parts of the roof of the hospital podium at Service Yard surroundings, that is known as the Finance Department extension Roof. The main generators will be located internally where the old generator from the early days of the hospital were housed (which is as the -2 floor known as the Service Level Floor) which now has been removed. As the generators have been removed, this projects is of urgent nature.
description:
The Royal Free Hospital London has experienced periods when the electrical supply from the external power supplier has been unavailable and needed to rely solely on the existing Standby Generator systems as a mean of providing Emergency backup power to meet the demands of the “Essential” electrical loads for critical patient areas. 

In addition, the service floor Generator system is part of the original building construction (circa 1970’s) & have reached their end of life as well as exceeding their power rating and is therefore operating at above their maximum capacity, hence cannot meet the demands of the existing “Essential” electrical loads. 

The impact to the community/public and Hospital critical patient areas is they will experience significant disruption in healthcare and potentially a risk to life during an Electrical Power outage without a suitable Back-up Emergency Power System.

The Hospital is therefore in urgent need of upgrading its Emergency Power Generator System to meet Statutory requirements and for the current and future demands of its critical services for patient care. This project will provide greater security of standby power to maintain vital clinical services through a new robust, reliable and more efficient back-up Emergency Power Standby Generator system. 

This project at Royal Free Hospital London, comprises the supply, delivery, offload and installation of new Generators, new Generator Flues new ventilation ductwork, new cooling systems, new ASCO MIMIC, Generator Status Panels, new Switchboards, new dual redundancy DC systems, , new CCTV and Access Control system, new lighting system in the room, new acoustic panelling and doors, new BMS system to upgrade with new equipment and replace some older equipment currently installed in Service Floor Generator Replacement Project (the part of the project which is internal and inside the hospital building). In addition to this, the project comprises the removal of existing Ductwork, Lighting, Switchboards and ad hoc equipment to create space for the new parts.

As part of the project there will be additional pieces of equipment and ductwork that would be placed externally to the Generator Room (the Generators are inside the hospital), at a location known as the Finance Roof which is the roof above the extension for the 'finance department extension', located at the Service Yard area. The Service Yard itself opens onto Fleet Road. 

It has to be noted that these generators and its associated external remote associated equipment will not constantly be running and only will operate in the case of an event of abnormal conditions such as an external loss of mains power (power cut) from the utility supplier or an internal electrical fault on site, and at times, for mandatory routine testing required by Electricity at Work Regulations 1989. In addition they will be turned on to be tested each year as per their maintenance programme.
